decision.question: review size
decision.why: weight.js, ai-cost.js and settings.js share one has_file (new weight/has-file.js) that asks the live folder names via a new async fetch_names in core/Router/listing.js; ai_cost runs on every page title

findings.text: `core/Router/listing.js:fetch_names` caches only after the response arrives, so the several `has_file` calls one page makes at once (weight, ai_cost, settings, each asking for 1-2 names) all miss the cache and each send their own `/api/folder-names` request; storing the in-flight promise in the cache would make it one request per folder.

`fetch_names` sets the shared `missing = true` on any non-JSON or non-ok answer, including the plugin's 403 for denied folder segments (`Server/plugins/FolderNames.js:28`), so one denied folder switches listing off for the whole session. This copies `names()` exactly as the brief asked, but it is a latent trap.

`has-file.js` keeps the full `directory.json` walk as the static-site fallback, which is what the brief asked for. On the live static site the stale tree still answers `false` for folders made after 2026-10-09, so failure 1 stays there (the log says so for the live check).

The requirements and the log line agree: 404s 85420 → 2437, Page tests and smoke (5 FAIL) unchanged, the three copies and `directory_tree()` removed, and a readme sentence added at `weight/readme.md:20`. No simpler design is needed; one shared async helper over the existing cache is the minimal fix.

answer.reply: noted: three same-origin 200s per page on the dev server only, each a few ms, then the 3 s cache; an in-flight map is more code than the requests cost. Worth it if a page ever asks many folders at once.

fixed: f9dcdf18f — a 403 now returns null for that one folder in both names() and fetch_names(), and never sets `missing`. Checked headless on qf-9: fetch_names('/.git/') is null, then fetch_names('/framework/core/Page/weight/') still lists has-file.js and names() still answers.

noted: off the dev server there is no live listing to ask, so the old tree is the only answer; the fix there is rebuilding directory.json at deploy, not this file. The dev site (monorepo.localhost) asks the live names, so failure 1 is gone where it was seen.
